Clipped text

The renewal window closes after fifteen months, and the late fee doubles on the first day after it closes.

This summary is clamped to two lines on purpose. The ellipsis at its end tells the reader there is more, which is the difference between a declared truncation and a hidden one.

A box with a fixed height and overflow hidden renders its first line and hides the rest without a scrollbar. Nothing errors, the text is in the document at full opacity, and a reader cannot get to it. This paragraph and the next exist so the page clears the blank-page floor.

The fix is to let the box grow with its content. Hiding the overflow is never the fix, because it is the defect.
